items.title: Claude produces first computer-checked proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem
items.body: Anthropic reports Claude completed an end-to-end Lean formalization of FLT in 11 days, writing 13 million lines and proving ~29,500 intermediate theorems. Kevin Buzzard reviewed it positively. This is the largest Lean proof yet and a concrete step toward AI-assisted verification of the mathematical literature.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra rolls out to Plus and Business users
items.body: Sam Altman and OpenAI confirmed GPT-6 Astra is now available to all Pro, Enterprise and Business Premium users in Work/Codex and the API; Plus and Business rollout completed overnight. Microsoft Azure also live. Pricing matches Fable 5.1 levels.

items.title: FLT formalization details and GitHub release
items.body: Claude agents used Prove2Me scaffolding and a multi-agent harness; the proof follows a simplified Darmon-Diamond-Taylor exposition of Wiles and was checked against Mathlib’s statement of FLT. Full Lean artifact is public.

items.title: Kevin Buzzard on the FLT autoformalization
items.body: Buzzard: ‘This extraordinary autoformalization achievement... proves Fermat’s Last Theorem with no assumptions other than the axioms of mathematics.’
